newsitem.title: USA: US 30-, 15-yr mortgage rates steady in week.
newsitem.headline: US 30-, 15-yr mortgage rates steady in week.

text.p: Average interest rates on U.S. 30- and 15-year fixed rate mortgages were rather steady in the week ending October 18 compared with the previous week, the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp said Thursday.
Freddie Mac said 30-year mortgages averaged 7.88 percent in the week, up only two basis points from 7.86 percent last week. Fifteen-year loans inched up in the week to 7.39 percent from 7.38 percent.
But adjustable rate mortgages fell to an average 5.62 percent from 5.68 percent in the week, it said.
A year ago, the 30-year rate averaged 7.38 percent, the 15-year 6.92 percent, and the ARM 5.72 percent.
"Interest rates remain steady and affordable this week, almost unchanged from last week," James Berkovec, principal chief economist for Freddie Mac, said.
"With low inflation and a healthy economy, now is an excellent time for homebuying," Berkovec added.
Earlier Thursday the Commerce Department said that U.S. September housing starts fell 6.0 percent after a 4.0 percent gain in August.
On Wednesday, the Labor Department said that U.S. September consumer prices rose 0.3 percent.

Freddie Mac said lenders charged an average 1.7 percent in fees and points on 30- and 15-year loans, unchanged from last week. They charged 1.4 percent on ARM loans, also unchanged from the previous week.
